events.border.night_crossing.title: The Late Booth
events.border.night_crossing.body: Two lanes, one open. The officer has been on since morning and it shows in how slowly he turns each page. Behind you an engine idles. Ahead, a strip light buzzes over a counter worn pale by other people's paperwork. He looks up, and waits.
events.border.night_crossing.out.waved_t: He reads every page anyway, stamps one, and slides the lot back without a word. The barrier lifts. Two hours of your evening, and nothing else.
events.border.night_crossing.out.held_an: He keeps the passport and asks you to wait. The wait becomes an office, and the office becomes a form. Nobody is unkind. It simply takes the rest of the night, and your name is written down twice.
events.border.night_crossing.out.papers_: He does not give the passport back. There is a receipt, a reference number, and an address to write to. He is already looking past you at the next vehicle.
events.border.night_crossing.out.underst: He opens the passport, closes it, and hands it back lighter. The barrier lifts before he has finished sitting down. Neither of you says anything worth writing down.
events.border.night_crossing.out.refused: He takes the note out, sets it on the counter between you, and looks at it until you take it back. Then he writes something. It takes a long time to write.
events.border.night_crossing.out.detaine: The note is still on the counter when the second officer arrives. There is a room with a bench in it, and a very long night, and by morning you are somebody they have a file on.
events.border.night_crossing.out.not_fou: He pats your coat twice, decides you are not worth the paperwork, and waves you on. You are three kilometres down the road before you breathe out.
events.border.night_crossing.out.found: He finds it on the second pass, without any particular triumph. It goes into a bag, the bag goes into a drawer, and you are told to wait while somebody senior is fetched.
events.border.night_crossing.out.small_t: You ask about the road ahead. He tells you, at length, which lane floods and which town has fuel. By the end he has forgotten to check the second page.
events.border.night_crossing.out.searche: He is not unfriendly. He is also thorough, and everything you own ends up on the counter in the order you packed it, then goes back in a worse one.
